Eat. Think. Smile's Oatmeal Raisin bars are a nice alternative to a mid-day candy bar. While perhaps not as tasty as something dipped in chocolate, the Eat. Think. Smile bars are baked and are relatively low in fat (7g, and only 1g saturated fat) although somewhat high in carbohydrates (34g) They also contain CocoaOne, which is described as "a unique blend of African cocoa and a premium Meso-American variety known ads Lavado," supposedly a natural antioxident.

Taste-wise, the Eat. Think. Smile bars taste much like a Cliff bar, and have the same shape and texture. The Eat Think Smile bars have a softer texture, and are more crumbly than a Cliff bar.
The oatmeal raisin taste is pleasant and not at all overwhelming.

Overall, I liked these bars. While not a replacement for a good breakfast or healthy lunch, these bars are perfect for that time of the day when you want a little snack, but don't necessarily want all of the fat and extras in a typical candy bar.

Summary: Great low calorie snack to tide you over hunger urges in between meals
Text: The Eat Think Smile Baked Nutrition Bar, Oatmeal Raisin, is a great low calorie nutrition bar/snack to tide you over hunger urges in between regular meals. At 1.8-ounce/200 calorie per bar, it is packed with different vitamins, minerals and fiber, from Vitamin A to Zinc, to supplement your daily nutritional requirements. Fiber content is around 7g per bar. I used mine basically as a pre-workout energy supplement to get that much needed energy to give you a push in your workouts. Be forewarned though that each bar has 200 calories, so if you stuff yourself up with 3 or more of this bar, for those of you that watches their caloric intake, this pretty much accelerates it, so moderation is the key when eating it. Just enough to tide you over those regular, more nutritious on time meals. A great snack, just don't over do it.

Summary: No replaqcement for a breakfast. but a great nutrition bar
Text:
I don't know how much thinking this requires.
This oatmeal raisin bar is a somewhat dry oatmeal raisin bar with a strong chocolate flavor. Somewhat like a dry, chewy brownie.
Definately low in fat, but not one of those diet bars.
More flavorful, more calories, more nutrition.

Summary: Good for Breakfast or a snack
Text:
A recent news story noted that Americans are skipping the traditional sit down breakfast for more on-the-go choices. Nuts, snack bars, etc. This is a perfect way to get healthful nutrition and a filling meal or snack on the go. It's a great blend of grans, raisins, and cocoa. It is a filling snack that will give you hours of energy. It tastes good, and not like the cardboard competitors. It also travels well, not melting or turning to mush as you go about your day.

Very tasty. I keep a few in my car, and in my office desk.

I eat a lot of Fiber One plus bars, usually 2 per day.
I know they are about 130 calories, but they rarely fill me like these seem too.

These Oatmeal Raisin bars from Eat, Think, Smile, are really soft and fresh, without the hardness of other bars.

These are very soft, and have a really hearty flavor. (not like the lighter rice cake taste of other bars, but not as heavy and sticky as Cliff bars)

I could eat these every day.

I enjoyed this nutrition bar, it tastes like a rich chocolate oatmeal raisin cookie. I found it to be very flavorful and the taste of rich cocoa really stood out for me. I think this is a good choice for a breakfast bar for those on the go. Of course I love nutrition bars and one concern I have is that people not use to nutrition bars may find this one a little dry, I also wish the bar was more moist and chewy. But I still enjoyed the flavor and ate them all. The bar is 200 calories, low in sodium 230mg has 34gm of carbohydrates and an excellent 7 grams of fiber. The bar only has 4gm of protein and I like to see them with at least 15 grams of protein. So with that said if it meets your nutritional guidelines I would recommend it.

Summary: 25% of Your Daily Fiber in a Healthy Snack
Text: Containing about 25% of the recommended daily intake of fiber, these bars are a fairly tasty way of obtaining it. However, don't expect an oatmeal raisin cookie type snack or a Larabar type snack either. It's dryer (meaning less fat/oil) than many snacks. It's also baked so it doesn't come across as a raw product either. The taste is pleasant and a bit more complex especially with the cocoa powder than many snacks. Finally, it's not an addictive snack which is good in that you won't be tempted to finish a box of these in three days. More health food than candy.

Summary: Cocoa and Walnuts, a Good Healthy Snack
Text:
Excellent healthy snack. Strong cocoa and cinnamon flavor with a walnut accent. Very filling.

Nutrition:
- 1.8oz/51g bar
- Calories: 200
- Fat Cal: 60
- Total Fat: 7g
- Trans Fat 0g
- Cholesterol: 10mg
- Sodium 230mg
- Total Carbs: 34g
- Protein: 4g
- Sugars: 12g
- 4% calcium,8% iron, 6% thiamin, 10% magnesium

Ingredients: Flour (whole wheat and whole grain corn), brown sugar, whole grain rolled oats, chicory root extract, canola oil, dextrose, walnuts, raisins, cocoa, brown rice syrup, glycerin, nonfat milk, 2% or less eggs, mono and diglycerides, cornstarch, salt, cinnamon, baking powder.

"Eat, Think, Smile" is offering a new and interesting variation on the standard granola br, a baked nutrition bar with all natural ingredients and an added dose of cocoa flavor. The cocoa is a natural antioxidant (who knew?), but it provides a nice finishing touch to the granola bar, like having cocoa sprinkled on top of your latte coffee. The granola bar itself is oatmeal raisin, with a nice chewy texture. This reviewer liked the taste.

The oatmeal raisin bar with cocoa comes one to a foil packet, rated at 200 calories each. The bars are available in boxes of twelve. Recommended as something a little different in a familiar snack.

Good bar that is not overly sweet.  It has a dryer than chewy granola texture and has less sticky feel.  It has good chocolate flavor, but not enough for me to get a "chocolate fix."  I felt full for a good length of time too which was nice.  I did not feel the need to eat a second one or eat again soon.
I love the taste, it is all natural, and the super Cocoa gives you a nice boost of energy and antioxidants.

About the only time I eat something like this is when I haven't allowed enough time for a proper breakfast before dashing out the door. These bars are tasty and filling without being overly sweet as some such products are. Yummy.

I love oatmeal and raisin anything, so I was really looking forward to trying these.  I wasn't disappointed.  The taste is a little more chocolatey than I prefer, but they're still good.  If you're looking for a yummy, thick oatmeal and raisin cookie snack, this is NOT it.  The taste of the oatmeal/raisins is fairly muted.  But if you're looking for something different (as well as healthy), and if the idea of a little chocolate mixed in with your oatmeal sounds good, give these a try.

Summary: Like the Convenience, But Not So Much the Taste
Text: I have eaten about 100 different type of food bars over the years since I don't always have time for breakfast or to leave work for lunch so when I saw these I wanted to try them out.  The picture on the box makes them look almost like a no bake cookie with lots of big oats and texture, but when I had my first one I was a bit disappointed since it was really more like a chocolate flavored sugar cookie with almost no texture.  The actual taste is mainly just a chocolate taste and the oatmeal and raisin might just barely come through on some bites.  I don't hate them, but they are certainly not my top pick.

Summary: Forget the Name.  Remember the Taste.
Text:
Don't the name throw you. "Eat. Think. Smile" isn't the easiest brand to remember, but their baked nutrition bars are certainly memorable in terms of taste. I tried two varieties through the Amazon Vine Program, Oatmeal Raisin and Orange Cranberry, and I loved them both. The bars are soft, chewy, sweet without being sugary, and decently sized (a little bigger than a Clif Bar, perfect for a between meal snack or a before-exercise pick-me-up). Best of all, they were satisfying without being too filling. I was a little doubtful about how the addition of cocoa would affect the flavors, but as it turned out, the cocoa was only detectable as a pleasant undertone and didn't overpower the Oatmeal Raisin or Orange Cranberry.

When deciding whether or not to recommend a food item I have sampled for free, I always ask myself, "Would I actually pay for this product?" In the case of "Eat. Think. Smile" nutrition bars, my answer was a resounding "Yes. I prefer these to some of the other bars I buy at the store." Therefore, I am pleased to be able to recommend them to you. Eat. Think. Smile. And enjoy.

Summary: Four and a half stars for this nutrition bar
Text:
There must be a million energy bars on the market, so what distinguishes this Eat/Think/Smile nutrition bar from its competitors? A not-too-sweet taste, for one thing.

As they say in the ads, the idea of a granola bar or an energy bar is to put good food stuffs in a convenient and tasty bar. This ETS (I'm already tired of typing in the full name!) bar is no different. What I like about it is that it has a solidly-good taste that means you're not going to chow down on it, but you're going to savor it, and take a few minutes to get through it. And that's a good thing as I'm concerned.

I not claiming it's going to change my like, but these are handy to stuff in the day pack for a trip to the mountains or the coast, and can be relied upon to get some good ingredients into your system.

Recommended, if for nothing more than the taste. I'll try another box soon. They are healthier than Girl Scout cookies, my go-to food in March.

Im nibbling one on of these as I'm typing. I like the taste, chocolatey, nutty, a standard 1.8 oz weight, long flat shape.

However, the downside of these bars. While it's a good taste, it's just simply not that filling. The consistency is very light. The light and airy taste doesn't leave me very satisfied after I've eaten it -- I want more substance.

Didn't care for it. Color is wrong, doesn't have the flavor. Tastes almost as if it were watered down, or, maybe, birch beer lite. Gonna have to try a different brand. I had pretty high hopes, too, as Pa. is the state where I first was exposed to birch beer. Can't recommend this brand. On the off chance that someone reads my reviews, I will sing loud praises when I find one to my taste.

I bought 2 12 packs of this for my granfather whom used to be able to buy it on post before they stopped carrying it. The shipping was fast and arrived in a timely manner. The bottles where all in good condition and tasted great, i myself had never had a birch beer before i got these for him and will have to say there way better than root beer!

These bars are GREAT!  Very tasty. No high fructose corn syrup.  I bought them for my toddler-age sons, both of whom really liked similar bars from Gerber and NutriGrain.  I was really shocked and disappointed to learn that those bars had high fructose corn syrup, though. (Seriously? A bar specifically for BABIES has HFCS?!)  So I opted for these.  They LOVE them, and so do I.  But I get them for 2.79/box locally. Even the most expensive grocery store around has them for 3.29/box.  I'm all for convenience, but we go through way too many boxes of these for it to be worth paying an extra fifty cents or a dollar (or more - price seems to vary by flavor here) more per box.

I love Kashi products.  I eat one of these every day.  The only complaint I have is with Amazon's price of this product and food products in general.  You can get this at local stores (you know the Red and the Blue one) for less than 3 dollars a box.

I love these Kashi bars, I used to get them at the local Walmart,but for some reason they stopped carrying them. I was looking around on the web to see where I could find them and found out that Amazon had them and at a great price. They are very delicious.

I love these cereal bars!  They are similar to Nutri-Grain but better.  These do not contain high-fructose corn syrup.  I paid $15.20 for the 6-pack with Subscribe & Save discount.  That's $2.53 per box which is cheaper than I can buy them on sale at the local grocery store.  Excellent value.

Summary: Perfect for toddlers on the go
Text: My 3-yr-old hates to sit at the table and eat breakfast, she always wants to take a snack in a cup and run around.  Most days, she would rather go without breakfast than sit down and eat.  I finally compromised and got her some Kashi cereal bars that she could eat on the go.  I was so pleased to find something with whole grains, real fruit and no high fructose corn syrup that I could give her.  She loves them, I love that she eats them and they are better for her than other bars on the market.  I wish they had more flavors than the three I'm always buying, I would purchase more to give her more variety!

I have loved Kashi cereal for years and recently found these bars, which are like some of the other cereal bars (NutriGrain?) I have had in the past, but from everything I can tell, seem to be of better quality. I think they work great as a snack or a quick breakfast. Better than a candy bar, but not as good a the raw fruit! :)

I'm becoming a big fan of Kashi for my family and these cereal bars are great! (And the apple ones, too.) My 20 month old has severe food allergies and kashi bars are one of the only easy things she can have for breakfast (meaning, if she doesn't have a kashi bar, I'll be whipping something up from scratch... and 20 month olds tend to like breakfast sooner rather than much later). So for our family, these are a staple.

Also, given that we live in the country, these are not available to us locally, so being able to buy them via amazon's subscription makes it VERY helpful for our family. (Unless amazon runs out and it takes them a month to get them in stock and delivered which kind of defeats to point of a subscription... *ahem*... amazon, you might want to work on that.)

Overall though, I'd recommend these! I love how healthy they are. I love how they have wholesome ingredients (that my daughter isn't allergic to). And I love that they have all that and still taste good! Thanks, Kashi!

My daughter loves fruit filled bars. I am not such a fan because of the sugar contant and unhealthy flour they use to make most of them. So I decided to try these (since they seemed like they would be healthier).

The taste is good. The size is good. The only drawback is that the bar is a little dry and cakey, almost like a bran muffin. The texture took a bit getting used to, but other than that the fruit bar is pretty good.

I enjoy most Kashi products, and this one is no exception.

Pros:
Tastes great, can taste fresh strawberries plus the whole grains.
Not too sweet.
No high fructose corn syrup.
No artificial ingredients.
Individually wrapped.

Cons:
They are a bit on the dry side.
A little more expensive than other cereal bars, but very much worth it.

Summary: My 17 year old son will eat these for breakfast.
Text: My 17 year old son will grab one of these as he leaves for school which makes me feel that he is getting something decent for breakfast. He enjoys the straberry flavor of the bar.
Shipped fast and packed well. This is a terrific cereal bar and low cal. It has a great taste and texture. everyone who tries them, loves them. Can't wait to try another flavor.

Summary: Yummy. Low calories and great taste
Text: Another great product for those looking for a "healthy" snack without a lot of calories

Summary: I love most kashi, but would skip these.
Text: I love most of the kashi products but I've now tried these and the cherry vanilla bars...the texture is a little off putting to me, almost like mushy graham cracker but with a less appealing taste (than graham) the fruit filling is almost bitter tasting to me (and yes these do have a lower sugar count, but I still don't want to eat bitter fruit) On a more important note, my boyfriend had one of these every day for about 5 days when he connected that they were giving him an upset stomach) now that could be an individual problem, perhaps something in them he is slightly allergic to, but he hasn't mentioned any of the other kashi products disturbing him. That being said, if you have a lot of food allergies I'd probably stay away from these, they aren't especially tasty and really they don't serve that much nutritional purpose anyhow...you'd be better served to eat some real strawberries.
The best Kashi bar flavor, tastes great, a awsome snack that does not taste like a bunch of processed food cardboard like bars.

Summary: Great, healthy breakfast bar that tastes great!
Text: These are very tasty and healthy! My toddler gets up in the morning and asks for "Bar" (breakfast bar) and devours them. It's great knowing she is getting a healthy start to her breakfast and loves the taste. She normally asks for "More bar?" but by then I have her fruit ready. Thank you, Kashi! Love the healthy, soft breakfast bars for kids. Hoping for more flavor options for the soft cereal bars soon!

I love the strawberry flavor of these.  I bought these with the Subscribe & Save discount and got them for a very reasonable price - $2.53 p/box.  The expiration date for all 6 boxes isn't until Sept 2012.  I can guarantee all of the cereal bars will be eaten way before then!  I had been buying the Nutragrain bars for our house but like a lot of parents, want to give the best foods to my son.  At the price I got through Amazon, I'm able to do that without hurting the bank.  Wish they would come out with more fruit flavors! (On a side note because I was dairy free for a year when my son was a baby & allergic to dairy... these are dairy free!)
They're good breakfast/snack bars... but they're very dry compared to the blackberry flavor. I probably won't be purchasing the strawberry again.
The kids really like these bars and you get a great price with the subscribe and save.  I like that fact that they don't use any high fructose corn syrup!

I love how these bars are so delicious and can be a quick breakfast or light snack. I am glad that Kashi has NO high frutose corn syrup in their products! It is hard to find healthy foods and snacks without corn syrup in it! I can't wait to try the other flavors offered.

Summary: Great for Fiber and a quick healthy snack
Text: I try to eat two of these per day, they are great for adding fiber to your diet and I really enjoy the taste.  I've only tried the strawberry flavor.  I subscribed to this item via Amazon prime.

I love all of the Kashi bars, from the granola nut type to these more breakfast type.  The flavors are really good and I really enjoy having choices that are different from the run of the mill chocolate, peanut butter, strawberry, blueberry that are so common in all of the other bars.  The pumpkin is one of my favorite and I love how the strawberry tastes more like the real thing than what seems more like a mere flavor in the other brands.

I love most of the Kashi products I've tried. This was low in sugar which is great right BUT when my kids tried it and refused to finish it I tried it and I now know why. It tastes horrible....it has a very weird funny taste to it.

Slightly more than 100 calories and packed with some fruit and whole grains, this makes for a great breakfast when you have very little time.  My son, Hubby and I like eating these quickly in the morning before rushing off to work.  They're easy to eat and yummy and make very little mess.  The only thing that would make me love them better is if they were organic.
I bought these for my kids.  I'm not fond of strawberry, so I can't comment directly on them, but they sure vanished quickly.  I think that says it all.
This cereal bar is kind of dry.  It is hard to eat without a drink nearby.  The taste is ok but not my favorite for sure.

Summary: The best of the novelty hot sauces.
Text: Great flavor, and HAWT! Trust me, this stuff delivers exactly what it says. Get an ice bath ready, and wear loose clothing. haw haw

SHAN spices are sold all over the country from 84c to 99c per pack at your local indian and Pakistani grocery stores.
This guy is just rip off and no justification for the over charge. Amazon should be aware of it. As Amazon is a good place to shop and I
do my shopping at Amazon and find prices very resonable.

Summary: Good mix if you don't have time or ingredients for homemade
Text: We like this mix when time is shorter or I don't have everything I need for chicken curry made from scratch.  It is a hot mix, but with Shan spice mixes you can use what you like, so if you're leery of the heat, I would suggest just using 1/4-1/2 a packet first. If you want it hotter next time, increase the amount.  I'm surprised at the price for this - we get these mixes locally for 99 cents a box.  Might want to check with the seller what quantity this price is for.

I love dark chocolate covered cranberries, and these were the worst I've ever had.  The chocolate was poor quality and tasted dry and waxy.  They are not "melt in you mouth" enjoyable as they should be.  Very disappointing.

I am sorry to hear the person before me was unsatisfied due to the food's origin, but for those of you that are looking at this as a care-free non-vegan, snacker.... MY FRIENDS AND I LOVE THEM (even my most vegan one who probably didn't do proper research..or did and didn't care enough to write a review about China and confront the company)! They taste great, fit into a bag on the go, and are much healthier to snack on at work than our usual vending machine goods. So whether it comes from an organic farm in the country or a NYC sewer... they taste awesome! I feel bad for the other person who is going to miss out on the yummy goodness of this snack....

Summary: Tastes Great but  Made in China
Text: Heads up to all of you out there who love Mrs. Mays.  I too love their products and was a regular customer. I liked the simplicity of ingredients, the fact that most of them were "organic" and that they were Vegan. I purchased a case of various items from them directly, and imagine my surprise when I noticed the box they arrived in said "A Product of China." I emailed them and they confirmed that their product is indeed produced in China. Having traveled in China, and, based on recent problems related to products made in China, I am no longer buying Mrs. Mays. How anyrhinf grown there could be described as "organic" strikes me as disingenous at best. The energy required to ship the product back to the US also strikes me as wasteful. I no longer purchase their product. When they produce their products with locally grown, organic ingredients, I'll be back!

Summary: can form part of a breakfast; cheaper elsewhere
Text:
These breakfast biscuits/cookies come in three flavors - oat, blueberry, and apple cinnamon. Each wrapped container contains four biscuits/cookies that are generously sized and oval shaped. The golden oat flavor reminded me of a graham cracker that had been paired with oats. The flavor was pleasant with a slightly sweet component. I think the product is best when paired with tea and a piece of fruit.

I did not experience increased energy and when eaten alone the product did not keep me full very long. When paired with a banana or apple and some almonds, I could see these cookies being used as part of a quick breakfast.

The product has a good bit of fat and sugar. As the product's nutritional profile is not presently listed, here is an abbreviated listing of one serving's nutrition:

Serving size: 1 package (four biscuits)
230 calories
8 grams of fat
.5 grams of saturated fat
2.5 grams of polyunsaturated fat
5 grams of monosaturated fat
220 mg. of sodium
85 mg of potassium
35 grams of carbohydrates
3 grams of dietary fiber
11 grams of sugar
4 grams of protein

Ingredients: whole grain blend (rolled oats, rye flakes), enriched flour [wheat flour, niacin, reduced iron, thiamin mononitrate (vitamin b1), riboflavin (vitamin b2), folic acid], high oleic canola oil, sugar, evaporated cane sugar, whole grain wheat flour, malt syrup (from corn and barley), invert sugar, baking soda, salt, soy lecithin, disodium pyrophosphate, datem, ferric orthophosphate (iron), niacinamide, pyridoxine hydrochloride (vitamin b6), riboflavin (vitamin b2), thiamin mononitrate (vitamin b1).

At present, these breakfast biscuits are definitely cheaper in grocery stores and Kraft has been issuing many dollar off coupons so check your local circular.

Allergy info: this product contains wheat and soy.

I just bought a few boxes of Belvita at a local store and I really love the golden oat variety. The taste and texture are so good I'd want to eat them whether they were "healthier" or not (I say "healthier" instead of "healthy" - because although they have no HFCF, contain whole grains and fiber, more "real" ingredients and better handling/baking, they are still a processed food). Anyway, I thought I'd see if amazon had a good deal on them. I'm floored by the price here! Over $25 for 3 boxes??? I think I only paid $2.99/box. Shop around, guys!

I can't say if it gives sustained energy as I just had my first pack.  I will say they were crisp and tasted great!  I'm always looking for portable energy food that is NOT low calorie.  These are about 230 calories per pack and since I take snacks like this hiking/backpacking, that's a good thing.  So far, I really like them.  Perhaps I'll update after I take them hiking and see how they hold up.

Summary: Perfect for breakfast on the go
Text:
Yes, I know that "breakfast is the most important meal of the day" yada, yada, but I, like many who start the day before the sun is up, don't really feel like eating first thing in the morning. By the time the early domestic tasks have been completed I am usually in the car rushing for work.
I have found these biscuits are a great way of starting the day and can be eaten just about anywhere (ok, not while swimming, obviously). There's a lot of calories and oats in there and to me they do seem to be better than a bagel or toast, keeping me going until lunch time.
Get them in your local store, as they are unbelievably expensive on line.

I love these little breakfast biscuits.  They are tasty, very filling and full of fiber, without tasting like cardboard.  I only eat 2, in a package and save the others for a snack.  If you like oatmeal cookies you will like these.  I don't care for the "blueberry" flavored ones, they are too artifical for me.

I LOVE THESE BELVITA BREAKFAST BISCUITS ALTHOUGH I WOULD CONSIDER THEM MORE OF
A COOKIE. I HAVE ONLY TRIED THE GOLDEN OAT AND THEY ARE VERY GOOD. I RATED THEM A FIVE STAR ON QUALITY AND TASTE.
ONE THING THAT I WOULD SUGGEST THAT AMAZON IMPROVE ON IS A LITTLE MORE CAUTION IN SHIPPING
AS I HAVE RECEIVED SOME THAT WERE HAD SOME BROKEN PIECES.

Summary: These little guys are so tasty!  I'll definitely be buying more!
Text: I purchased these several weeks ago and put them at my desk at work for breaksfast on the go.  I've been putting off trying them because I wasn't sure if they would taste like cardboard.  Opened a pack today and was pleasantly surprised!  Will definitely be buying some more.  They taste like a yummy version of a graham cracker.
These are the best breakfast crackers ever!!! A light spread of crunchy peanut butter and you're good to go.  Very tasty and good for you.  What's not to love?
This is one of the best habanero hot sauces out. It has a slight vinegar taste to it, but not overpowering. The flavor is phenomenal!

This is not like any traditional English pudding.  In fact, it is unlike anything I've ever attempted to put in my mouth.  It is pumpkin in color, springy in texture, with globs of stretchy substance which I suppose is the treacle.  I am at a loss to describe the flavor - a sweetness lingers in the background, but what the prevalent taste is I don't know.  It's not buttery, salty, caramelized...it's 'misc.' flavor.  My husband and I each took a bite or two, had a good laugh, and tossed the rest.  We're not fussy food snobs, nor are we unsophisticated eaters.  My husband's best contribution to my attempt at analysis was "if someone told me that was monkey brains, I'd seriously believe them."

When this canned dessert arrived I could hardly wait to open it and try it out but I waited till my son was over and we enjoyed it together! I tasted it cold (got on my fingers while pushing it from the can) and found it very tasty and reminded me of pumpkin. It is supposed to be heated and was very easily done in my microwave. We both liked it heated but I still like it better cold. If you like something sweet, you have to give this a try!
I remember real treacle pudding from when I was little and lived in England.  This canned version is terrible.  It's nothing like the real thing. Don't waste your money.
I bought Heinz Treacle Pudding mainly out of curiosity having heard of it for years but never tasted it. I found it was quite good and will have it again.

Not bad for a canned dessert. I used some whipped cream because it was a little dry.

I was surprised upon opening this that the inside of the can isn't lined. I think some can flavor may have leached into the taste, affecting the flavor (or is that "flavour"?)

Like any other food, not every treacle pudding will taste exactly the same.  Personally, I like this better than a number of restaurants' treacle pudding.  And what do you expect from buying canned food? For what it is (cake in a can), this stuff is great.

Summary: Eating these since I was a kid...
Text:
These little packets carry 4 'leafs' of seaweed... to mee they are kindof like potato chips, salty, cruchy, and wonderful! I've been eating them since I was a kid! A great low-calorie snack for dieters.

In case you are curious, here's some of the nutritional info per packet:
Calories: 1.333
Fat: 0
High in vitamins: iron, calcium, vitamin A, B1, B2, & C

Summary: I have loved these since I was a kid. They are just awesome!!!!
Text: I have loved these since I was a kid. They are just awesome!!!! I started to buy these locally at one of the oriental stores (locally meaning a half hour drive - lol). Unfortunately The store I buy such products from had been shut down and there was no other local oriental store from which I could buy my favorite foods. Although shipping is a bit costly, it's not so bad if you buy a ton of packages at once, thus saving you on shipping costs. Being that I spent 2 years in Japan, I am addicted to quite a few of the foods they make there and this seaweed is an addiction for me. I just love it and I could eat 10 packets of these at once. You must try these seaweed packets. Don't be fooled by the other seaweed products. These are specific, slightly salted, excellent munchy snacks, even taste more wonderful than potato chips, pretzels or anything else. They have less calories. You just cannot go wrong with these wonderful seaweed snacks. If you don't buy these you really are missing out on the awesome foods in life.  XD

Summary: Ate some of it, threw most of it away
Text: I love roasted seaweed, and had purchased the Sea's brand on amazon several times. I wanted to branch out and maybe get a better bang for my buck so I tried these. They didn't compare. The seaweed itself was all stale; it lacked the crunch of other roasted seaweed. I supposed I could have tried adding strips to soup or something, but I really just wanted something I enjoy eating directly. I don't know if I just got a bad bag, but I don't think I'm going to try another one. Too bad, I loved the idea of the small wrapped portions that would fit in the pocket.
THIS IS A GREAT PRODUCT, I PUT THEM IN WITH THE  NOODLES JUST BEFORE  I STRAINE THE WATER OUT(CUT THEM INTO PIECES)LET IT STAND FOR  A MINUTE AND ITS GOOD TO GO, IT WILL JAZZ UP ANY PLAIN SOUP,
I was disappointed with this product. I like my seaweed snack thin and crispy. It was chewy. Not happy at all.

Text: Matsutani Ajitsuke seaweed comes in small packs, which are very handy if you are using these to manage a food or cigarette craving, or to include in kids' lunches if you have open-minded offspring. However, the taste and texture are subpar. These are thicker and tougher than they should be, with a distinct taste of soy sauce. They do not dissolve on the tongue as nicely as competitors' products do. I got through one of the 100 packs in the Amazon shipment but I plan to give the rest away if I can.

Summary: not Korean seaweed snack... learn the difference!
Text: I'm an avid fan of both the Korean seaweed snacks as well as the Japanese seaweed snacks. This, being the Japanese seaweed snack, is chewier, less oily and less salty than the Korean counterpart because it's not roasted but simply dried. The people who bought this and gave it negative reviews because they thought it was stale don't know the difference between two. This is a great snack if you really enjoy the taste of seaweed and are looking for something more "plain". It's always a good idea to know what you're buying before you buy it and give it negative reviews!

Summary: Pomegranate in the name is deceiving
Text: I purchased these treats on Amazon thinking they would be like the chocolate covered pomegranate seeds at Trader Joe's, but unfortunately they are not. While they are quite tasty (yes, I will be finishing the bag!), the expectation was that there was actually going to be pomegranate as the main ingredient. The name is misleading and, like many food companies, this seller is jumping on the bandwagon of adding the smallest amount of the fruit in the mix and using its name in the title. The pomegranate juice concentrate is mixed with several other fruit juices, and there is no indication on the package of how much pomegranate is actually in there. Trader Joe's version is actual pomegranate arils covered in a small amount of chocolate - definitely could qualify as a "healthier" treat option. These, unfortunately, do not. Quite tasty, but don't kid yourself on any health benefits here - too much sugar! FYI: 180 calories and 26 grams of sugar in ¼ cup (about 16-20 nuggets).

I just discovered this candy at Walmart and only bought one bag to see how I liked it. I wish I'd bought more!  I love almost any combination of fruit and chocolate and these sweet-but-tart little morsels are a superb example of how delicious that blend can be.  Walmart's price is currently the best by a large margin, so off I go to stock up on my latest confectionary addiction!

Summary: Perfect blend of tart and sweet
Text: I got some of these chocolates in December, and just ordered a replacement bag (because two pounds of chocolate should not be consumed quickly :). They are fantastic. It is high quality chocolate (nothing chalky or waxy) and tart pomegrante juice. 20 pieces to a serving, giving you 180 calories and 65 calories from fat.

I've yet to run into a product where, after sampling, I'm asked to go buy more for the office multiple months later. Add to that the boderline health benefits that come from the dark chocolate and fuit filling, and you have the best of both worlds. The tartness of the fruit begins to overpower much of the flavor later, so you can't have more than a small handful, but they're so rich, you won't want to anyway.

Summary: Brookside Dark Chocolate Pomegranate are Delicious
Text: I started eating this when Costco carried them and then they disappeared - I guess they're considered "seasonal".  Well, I love these little sweet tooth satisfiers all year long - pop 5 of these and you're good to go!
Considering I don't like pomegranate or dark chocolate individually, I was very surprised to learn that combining the two ingredients created a delicious chocolate treat!

Summary: Hands-down, the most delicious chocolate candies EVER MADE!!!!
Text: Words cannot describe how good these are. AMAZING. I used to buy the 12 oz bag from Wal-Mart, but then discovered you can buy a 2-lb bag from Sam's Club for only $10! Such a great deal! But I'm sure the bag I just bought will be gone within the next week : )

If you love chocolate and fruits, this is the product for you. I have just finished my first bag, and I still can't get over the taste. The candies are bite-size, and (even though I hate using cliches) you simply can't get enough of them. The chocolate doesn't taste bitter, but it's not too sweet either, and the pomegranate enhances the flavor with a slightly sour touch. Overall, just like those commercials say, your mouth will thank you.

Don't order chocolate in the summer! Because I had experienced the pomegranate/chocolate pieced before, I know the product is yummy, but the little nuggets had been turned into one big chunk of crumbly chocolate by the time it arrived at my house. Very disappointing.

I love chocolate -- rich, dark, lucious chocolate, and every autumn my love becomes an obsession. For most of the year, I am able to have a bite of good chocolate candy or a rich chocolate pie or ice cream once a month or so, and it is enough. Not as much as I want, but as much as I need, and I'm satisfied. However, as the days cool and get shorter during the autumn, my craving is impossible for me to withstand, and I have always laid in a big supply of Hersheys and mini M&Ms, etc, for Halloween, and then I "graze" on the leftovers for the next six weeks. How long has it been since you have actually TASTED one of these products, rather than just eaten them remembering "you always liked them." When you taste it, you taste a lot of sweet but very little chocolate, and so I'm not satisfied.

So, wanting to find a healthier snack in the hope of appeasing these urges, I tried these.

Living in Texas, I ordered these during the first solid "cool spell" of fall, which was a mistake. By the time they were shipped and arrived, we had another streak of near-hundred degree days, and so the product arrived and had melted in shipment and re-congealed into a mostly-amorphous mass after arrival. When I opened it, I was irritated at first, but then I realized this was actually a confirmation that I was dealing with a better grade of chocolate, so I carefully extracted the lump and put it on a cutting board, prying the mass apart with a chef's knife.

Under a little pressure, the lump broke apart into smaller lumps, but there were a substantial number of the "beads" of chocolate which came apart, reflecting the original consistency of the product, so I tasted them. The flavor, and the combination of pomegrante and the rich Brookside Dark chocolate was amazing. The aroma as you brought it to your mouth, and the release of the vibrant flavors "sang" to whatever area of my brain craves chocolate. 3 small pieces with a small glass of milk, and I was happy.

I love chocolate, and I love pomegranate, but who knew what a synergy there is between these flavors! (I love chocolate covered orange peel, and enjoy chocolate dipped raspberries or strawberries, but they are not very significant compared to these small nuggets of chocolate.) As someone married to a creative cook, I can imagine a cheesecake topped with a vanilla and sourcream topping, with these dotting the top rather than the bland white chocolate chips.

Back to my story -- just 3 of these with a little milk, and I was both ecstatic and content. I cannot wait to try 2-3 with a fine cup of dark coffee after a meal. I'm not sure how many callories are in one of these, but my guess is the two or three which satisfies is no more than a "mini" chocolate bar, and the flavor lingers in your mouth for minutes.

So, to recap, there should be all of the benefits of flavinoids of dark chocolate and pomegranate, and the flavors are rich enough to really register on the palate and brain. In a reasonable and small quantity, they are a "little taste of heaven", that satisfies my brain without blowing my diet!

You should order these if you prefer just a little excellent, flavorful chocolate, to a lot of so-so choclolate. Maybe they'll work for you like they are for me. Just make sure the weather is cool before ordering! Since ordering in hot weather was "on me", five stars for this fine product.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

my 2 bags of dark chocolate covered pomegranate came to me melted into two blocks of chocolate and pomegranate. of course, this also means that the chocolate was dried out. i am going to see if my costco still carries these candies and not buy them by mail again, if i can help it. the box they were shipped in was not even labeled as to special handling of the contents. very poor shipping, amazon.

the product gets 5 stars. the (super saver) shipping and handling gets no stars. i guess i got what i paid for.

ellen

Summary: If you like dark chocolate and even if you don't these are delicous
Text: Delicious candy. When you look at the ingredients they seem much healthier than most chocolates but It is candy though not a health snack. My problem with them is I just can't stop eating them till they are all gone.

This flavored chocolate confection is merely okay.

First off, it isn't really chocolate over pomegranate seeds. That would have been cool. Instead it is chocolate that supposedly has the flavoring from a different confection from the same manufacturer, and that confection supposedly tastes something like pomegranate. That stuff is mixed into dark chocolate to make this stuff.

The dark chocolate part of this confection isn't semi-sweet, which is what I'm used to seeing for dark chocolate, instead its regular sweet, making it too sweet.

Some of the confection appears to have that beige dimpling that occurs when chocolate, particularly dark chocolate, is exposed to the elements. I don't know if its water, or air that does that, but this package was like that.

Many of the small balls were stuck together into large constellations.

All in all this confection isn't disgusting, but it hardly deserves the rank it has. I'd say all in all its pretty 3-star average.

EXCEPT, this treat has a fatal flaw: it doesn't taste like pomegranate. Not even a little bit. Nope, no trace of pomegranate flavor is perceptible. It tastes like not-pomegranate. And that not-pomegranate taste isn't readily identifiable. I eat fresh pomegranates regularly, and so have an inkling of their flavor, and that pomegranate-flavor isn't contained within this chocolate confection.

Summary: Things that didn't occur to me... chocolate melts
Text: Delicious product.  However, be aware of where you live and what the season is.  I ordered these in June in North Carolina and they arrived as a bag of liquid chocolate with suspended animation pomegranate seeds.  Put them in the freezer and then had a chocolate and pomegranate brick.  Still was able to enjoy them by breaking off pieces and making cookies (oatmeal raisin cookies that have chocolatey pomegranate instead of raisins).  Very good cookies.
We are watching what we eat and these prove to be a very satisfying and WONDERFUL snack, while the dark chocolate and Pomegranate anti-oxidants help our health!  LOVE THEM!

I absolutely detest dark chocolate, so when someone gave me these as a gift I was bitterly disappointed. But I couldn't very well throw out this large bag without giving these a try so I ripped it open and took a nibble. My reaction? Holy cow, are these delicious! The dark chocolate covering was nowhere as bitter tasting as I'd feared and it went well with the sweetened internal "juice piece." Now I and the rest of the household are hopeless addicts, because they're just that good.

BTW, let's talk about the controversial "juice piece" that other reviewers are mentioning. Just know that when you buy these Brookside candies (blueberry, pomegranate, acai), that the "fruit" in the middle isn't a whole dried fruit; it's some kind of concoction that's a blend of several juice pieces. Some people have described this as being "like jelly" but that's inaccurate. The candy has the exact consistency of chocolate-covered raisins, so in spite of the artificiality of the juice piece, there's nothing particularly funky or fake-ish about the texture that should cause anyone pause. I personally didn't have an issue with the fact that these are "fruit pieces" but some people wanting the "real thing" might want to be aware of what they're getting should they order a bag of these.

One last good thing about these Brookside chocolates? They're very filling. Just a small handful and you're stuffed. So there's no danger of gorging on them like you would a less healthy candy. So all in all, a very good product and welcome, much healthier alternative to the usual fare. Just a word of advice: if you're a member of Costco's or BJ's, you're better off buying these over there, because these stores sell them for much cheaper (a little under $10).

Summary: Best candy ever! Beware, they are addictive
Text: After finishing five bags over the last year, I was hoarding my supply as Costco has stopped carrying the pomegraniate variety. The Acai are not nearly as good, as the tangy pomagranate compliments the dark chocolate so well. Do not hesitate to buy these, the chocolate is great, total flavor sensational.
I'm pretty sure they put crack in these because it is impossible to stop eating them.  This is my third bag and it's disappearing at an alarming rate! Love it.

Brookside Dark Chocolate Covered Pomegranates 2lb Bag
Usually I get good prices on Amazon but this product was purchased for me from Costco and paid $8.00 less than Amazon. Product is delicious but I could purchase 2 - 2 lb bags for the price of one on Amazon. Sorry.

The chocolate covered pomegranates are luscious.  Wonderful dark chocolate covering these chewy-center candies can't be too bad for you, what with dark chocolate and pomegranates both healthy foods!  They are a little smaller than an M&M Peanut candy, so they would not be appropriate for very young children, so Moms have an excuse to not share. These are a delicious tart but sweet candy.  I purchased a bag on a whim and they were loved by everyone in my family.  I doubt they have much nutritious value but they are a tasty treat.

Summary: MMMMmmm good!  Love those little balls!
Text: Love these pomegranate balls!  Can't find them everywhere and definitely not in a package this big!!  Bonus!  They satisfy a chocolate craving and they are fruity and chewy.

Someone brought this to the beach as a 'hostess' gift.  My heavens,  I am not sure how we functioned before we had these in our life.  Just a few of these assuages an insistent sweet tooth, for not too many calories.  (We never actually eat a whole serving at one time.)  I am ordering more of these - They are more fun to take as a house gift than a bottle of wine.  Everyone I have given them to loves them!

It has gotten so bad in our household that we have to hide the bag from ourselves. We never miss a week without having a bag of these treats on hand. It has gotten worse because now we can find the chocholate pomegrantes even at Walgreens! Help! They are shamefully delicious and impossible to avoid.

I make sure to keep these in the house because I have huge chocolate cravings and don't feel bad for eating these. They are not super sweet but satisfy that craving, and much "healthier" than a Hershey bar. I get them at BJ's wholesale club for around $10. They are fun to pop in your mouth and everyone I know who has tried them thinks they are great.

I must warn you, these are highly addictive. We're going through our 3d bag now. The taste is so wonderful that when your bag's over, you don't simply want something sweet, you want THEM. The outside dark chocolate is not too sweet and not too bitter - just right to go with the filling (the filling has almost the same texture as the chocolate, it's not liquid or caramel-ish). Costco sells it for a little over $9 for this 2 lbs bag. The candy is completely natural, no artificial anything, no preservatives. Highly highly highly recommended, but... did I mention it's addictive?

I actually bought these at Costco and was just curisous to see others opions. Was really suprised to find so many good review! For me the jelly center was a no go but to each there own. I should have looked closer at the package.
I bought this product for the health benefits of dark chocolate and pomegranate.  I believe, eaten in moderation, it can be a healthy chocolate treat.

Product is delicious.  However we ordered the last shipment in July. Since the hot weather we recieved the item in chunk form as it had melted and stuck together rendering it unedible.  Recommend this item but not for shipment in hot weather.

bought these at costco for a few cents less and figure they will either double in price or never be in stock again glad to know they are here on amazon  They ARE addictingly good..the deep dark chocolate flavor is haunting.  I was looking for choc cherries but these will do nicely

Summary: I never liked dark chocolate until I tried this
Text: Dark chocolate has always tasted bitter to me, so I've avoided it even though everyone keeps raving about the antioxidants in dark chocolate. I saw this in a local grocery store, and bought it on a whim. Wow! The ying / yang of (less sweet) dark chocolate to the (more sweet) pomegranate is irresistible. Let's just say that my local grocery store offers only a small pack, and Amazon has a giant 32 oz pack at a less expensive price. Enough said. LOL

Summary: Bet  you can't eat just one of these.
Text: These are awesome little dark chocolate covered chewy pomegranate candies.  Average size is about like a peanut M&M candy.  Wonderful, can't think of a bad thing to say about them except that the bag always empties too soon.  Great to have on hand (if you can keep them that long) for when company comes over. I pick them up at Costco where the price is better. What a treat!

Summary: Florida+Chocolate+July = one big two pound block of brown stickyness
Text: I should have known better than to order chocolate this time of year.  Most shippers refuse to ship chocolate to Florida in the summer.  As a Prime member I thought it might have been packaged well enough to get here in good shape.  There was nothing in the package to protect it from the heat and what should have been delightful little bites of chocolate covered pomegranate turned out to be a two pound block of chocolate with little bits of 'gummy' candy discs.  They may have been made with some pomegranate juice but not enough to give it that 'kick' that real pomegranate juice has.  Even if I see them on a shelf in a store and I can tell from feeling the package that they have not all melted together, I wouldn't spend this much money for so little pomegranate.
What was I thinking ordering these in the middle of summer. Bought as a gift, and it was melted into a sold block of chocolate when she received it. I was so embarrassed.

This is a wonderful product, we all love these at work, which is why I bought the 2 lb bag. But somewhere along the way it got overheated and all melted together in a big ball. Ruined the chocolate and ended up throwing it away. I guess don't order in the summer or come up with another shipping solution.

Summary: Yummy, Yummy In My Tummy - Chapter two!
Text: Oh boy! Here I go again praising the delicious candy made by Brookside. This one is in my opinion just a little bit better then the Blueberry flavor. My family tried "Brookside Dark Chocolate Covered Pomegranates 2lb Bag" and fell in love with this candy. Mix these in a salty trail-mix and you have something special for a hike or eat them straight out of the bag. Great snack. We all love this product. I found this product at Costco for the low price of $9.59. Recommended! Enjoy!

Summary: Apparently you can get these at Wal Mart too???
Text: Well, I have never seen them at our local Wal Mart and it may be a regional thing, but these little round chocolate morsels, about the size of a peanut m&m have the combined tastes of pomegranate and dark chocolate and they are GOOD!!!  Easy on them and enjoy in moderation, and with a 2lb pack they oughta last you a while if you only have say 4-5 a day tops.  Lots of sugar I'm sure but treat yourself nice every now and then.  I think you will really enjoy them but be careful if ordering in a hot climate...Some reviewers reported a melted mess.  Ours arrived perfectly fine and well packaged in a box and did not appear melted or congealed and we live in the Houston Texas area and it is mid July.  Go figure huh?

I do not generally prefer dark chocolate or pomegranate, but this product is AMAZING! The company is able to combine two things and make them taste even better. I can't just eat one and it's a party for your mouth.

What a delightful little treat. If you are a "I need a little sweet" person and want just a BIT of yummy to pop in your mouth these are totally satisfying because they have a bit of kick. But the true win in a household of athletes is adding them to trail-mix. If it is hot- They will melt and then glob together with all the other items. These are a delightful little add-in to really upgrade the quality of average trail-mix.

The combination flavor of dark chocolate & pomegranates is simply delightful & there is no way you can eat just one. . . before you know it, the bag vanishes!!  So, now I order at least 4 bags at a time - they are perfect for gifts & I have used them for dessert, instead of cake, and they just satisfy the craving for something sweet perfectly!  If you are craving chocolate, this is the perfect solution - your taste buds will thank you ~!~
Best candy I've had in a long time! Kind of expensive but good for special occasions. I don't know know about the nutrition value of this candy, but it does taste exceptional!

I want the snacks for my own consumption and for my little boy (3 1/2 years old). Recently, I found these Brookside Dark Chocolate Covered Pomegranates at my nearby Costco store. They're excellent in taste, as good a chocolate as you can generally find. They're sweetened with fruit juices, especially pomegranate. They're a dark chocolate and are a natural source of antioxidants. Did I mention that they're really, really good tasting? Did I mention that they're not particularly expensive? This is one item that fits the bill. The only difficulty is that they're so good you may have to worry about eating too many of them.

Gary Peterson

I usually like darker chocolate, but for some reason, the milkiness in this is perfect. But they truly are to die for.

however, the price I paid thru Amazon order was around $16 each. my daughter bought me some at

Summary: Good taste but not so great packaging......Buy with some reservation
Text:
I have always enjoyed Orville Redenbacher brand popcorns, whether it is SmartPop or Natural or Sweet & Savory type. And with such past experiences, I went ahead and bought this particular popcorn (Pop-Up Bowl Butter Microwave Popcorn), even though this particular product is way more expensive than the bag version.

First impression: Packaging looks great and the illustration on the box lures you to try it at once as soon as you look at the box.

Cooking: I used my Sharp microwave 1200 W, 1.2 cubic feet of sheer raw cooking power. Even though my microwave has sensor based cooking feature for popcorn and other food items, I set the microwave timer to 2 minutes and 30 seconds, so as to not leave anything to chance. Instructions on the pack are very clear about up & down side markings, cooking time, handling instructions etc. After cooking for 2 & 1/2 minutes, I carefully removed the popcorn bowl (as it miraculously transforms itself into).
Now comes the little tricky part. Instruction on the bowl clearly indicates how to handle the bowl and how to remove the top plastic off the bowl, so as to dig in and help yourself with the buttery popcorn. So I tried opening the bowl by pulling the plastic from one side, but to no avail. So I tried the other side with more frustration and no better result. I contemplated using a scissor to cut the plastic open, but then I would have to clean the scissor, since all the residual butter would be transferred to the scissor creating a mess. I was surprised that all this hype and commercial about bowl popcorn really amounts to such bad packaging. Then, I forcefully pried open the plastic and got hot residual vapors on my fingers. Boy, what a scalding experience it was!! But I endured the agony so as to try this new popcorn.

Taste: Popcorn kernels were large and uniform, and so were popped popcorn. It smelled very buttery, very aromatic indeed. They were crunchy, buttery and crisp. However, I could not have distinguished this final product from the regular Orville Redenbacher popcorns from regular paper bags.

Conclusion: If this product tastes the same as regular same brand paper bag product, why am I spending 3 times more money to buy this item? So that I could just eat from a bowl instead of a paper bag? Now I am not a dodo and neither are regular Amazon customers looking for a better bang for their buck, so then what on the earth would make one shell out more money? I am amazed at the marketing department at work here. Do they really think that giving people bowl instead of a paper bag would somehow cast a Harry Potter like spell on us and force us to buy this product on a regular basis? Well guess again marketing guys, as far as I am concerned, No Popcorn Bowl for me. If you like the idea of eating your popcorn from a paper bowl, and if you are willing to put up with the inconvenience and mess and higher price, then this is the product for you.

Pros:
1) Clear instructions
2) Tempting packaging
3) Giant uniform popcorn

Cons:
1) EXPENSIVE
2) No easy way to tear apart the plastic top off the final popcorn bowl
3) Did I mention EXPENSIVE

The idea of a popcorn bag that turns into a bowl is simply brilliant! I was sick of having to either get my hands covered with grease or clean the large bowl I'd dump my popcorn into. So I got these as soon as I saw them in the grocery store. Here are the problems;
What's worse than a hot, oily paper bag? Very hot, oily PLASTIC. The plastic absorbs heat more than paper, and it's the part you're expected to pull off to get to the popcorn! Ouch! Burnt my fingers more than once, and when I didn't, had to wait and let it get cold-ish.
The bowl is made of the same paper as the bag, and more flimsy, so you don't avoid getting grease everywhere. Unlike the bag, the bowl does not contain the popcorn. The popcorn reaches the very top of the bowl and falls out.
I'm going back to bags.

Summary: Sprayed orange grease all over the inside of the microwave
Text:
The pop-up bowl sounds like a great idea, but evidently they rushed it to market before all the bugs were out.

The first bag I cooked was fine, except the instructions for opening the bag are far from clear, and even after you figure out how to do it it's a lot of trouble and makes a big mess.

But the second bag evidently sprang a leak - it sprayed bright orange grease all over the inside of my microwave, even into the tiny vent holes inside the top and side. I always watch popcorn carefully while it pops, but I could not see the grease spray until after it was done and I opened the door. Cleaning it all out was a horrible ordeal, and I'm sure everything I cook in the microwave will come out smelling like popcorn grease for weeks.

They released this product too soon. It needs serious redesign. I will not buy it again.

Summary: Guaranteed to Burn Your Popcorn Every Time...
Text: There is a warning on the package not to use the popcorn button on the microwave.  First of all, why would they create popcorn that cannot use the convenient popcorn button?  The recommended cooking time is 2 to 2 1/2 minutes.  Follow the direction, and the popcorn in the middle is burnt every single time.  I am switching to Pop Weaver.

Good idea but sadly the product does not deliver. The bag is hard to open without burning your fingers or making a mess and most times the popcorn in the middle of the bag is burnt. (I have followed instructions and tried a few different time settings) I also think it leaves a  bit more of a greasy filmy residue on my tongue than other  microwave popcorns.
This "bowl" type is not very good. It leaves at least two dozed or more unpopped kernels. The bagged popcorn is far better. I usually get ten or less unpopped kernels in those.
It's more expensive, you get less product and I can't open the "bowl" without making a mess.  Back to bags please!

Sorry, the flimsy bowls are terrible you cannot pick them up and are not easy to handle. My favorite was Orville Tender White in the bag, they should offer both, but it appears Orville has switched to bowls only which you cannot pass to another person. I regret that I have switched to Jolly Time White and Buttery, Crispy White and any other brand still offered in bags! :(

I have always thought that Orville Redenbacher's is the best microwave popcorn. Until this product came along. It is a failure in several ways. If you pop for even as short as 2 1/2 minutes, you will get about 50% good kernals, and the rest will be burnt. And I mean individual burnt kernals and a few solid masses of burnt kernals fused together! I have popped three bags so far and the result has been the same for all three. And I stood next to the microwave listening, as the product advises. At 2 1/2 minutes, there was still plenty of popping going on, but I stopped anyway.

Then comes the challenge of opening the bag. The instructions are somewhat clear, but I was scratching my head on the first one or two that I popped. When you attempt to pull off the plastic bowl cover, you must pull very hard, and when you do that, the paper attached to the plastic tears and popcorn spills out. I tried pulling one side, but it didn't open cleanly, so I tried the other side, with the same result. I was determined not to use scissors because I didn't want greasy scissors that I would have to clean. I ended up on all three bags eating the popcorn with the plastic cover still partially attached. It was clear that any more attempts to remove the cover would have meant popcorn on the counter and floor.

Finally, the picture on the box showing a nice buttery yellow bag of popcorn overflowing the top of the bowl is blatant false advertising. On all three bags I popped - at the proper time and temperature - the result was some yellow kernals, some grayish kernals (on their way to being burnt), and black, burnt kernals. And each time, the amount of popcorn was at least two inches below the top of the bowl. And many kernals were not popped.

If an industrial design student presented this pop-up bowl for a class assignment, I think they would get an A minus for idea, and a D minus for execution. Didn't anyone at ConAgra foods bother to TEST this product before putting it on the market???

Summary: Messy, difficult to use new bag. Less popcorn.
Text:

Cons:

The plastic pop-up bowl packaging doesn't work very well. It's difficult to open. If you're not careful you'll end up spilling the popcorn all over the place while trying to open the bag. You might also burn yourself.

I know some people like to eat out of the bag, and if you do you will find this experience quite messy. The plastic portion of the bag does not soak up the oil like a traditional paper bag, so it gets all over your hands.

After popping 4 bags in 2 different microwaves, I have come to the conclusion that these new bags simply do not pop as well as the old ones. I have more unpopped kernels, and visibly less popcorn when I pour it out into a separate bowl to eat (which I prefer). And 1 of the 4 bags leaked some oil into the microwave.

The new bags are smaller than the old ones; 2.69 ounces compared to 2.9 (which used to be 3.3 ounces not too long ago.) Is this new packaging really just a scheme to hide a price increase?

Verdict:

2 stars.

Start with 4 stars for the taste; about as good as microwave popcorn gets, but not as good as homemade. Subtract 1 star for the smaller package, and another for the messy new bag.
